Traditional Glühwein

Served at: St. Nicholas Day

Serves 6-8Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Glühwein, or German mulled wine, is a quintessential warm beverage enjoyed throughout the Advent season, making it a perfect festive drink for St. Nicholas Day celebrations. Its aromatic spices and comforting warmth embody the spirit of winter holidays, often served at Christmas markets and family gatherings as a delightful treat.

Ingredients

  • 2 (750 ml) bottles dry red wine (such as Merlot or Spätburgunder)
  • 1 large orange, thinly sliced
  • 4 cinnamon sticks
  • 8 whole cloves
  • 2-3 star anise pods
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, or to taste
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) brandy or rum (optional)

Method

  1. Combine the red wine, orange slices, cinnamon sticks, whole cloves, star anise pods, and granulated sugar in a large non-reactive pot or Dutch oven.
  2. Stir gently to dissolve the sugar.
  3. Heat the mixture over medium-low heat. Do not let it boil; the goal is to gently warm the wine and allow the spices to infuse.
  4. Continue to heat for about 15-20 minutes, or until the Glühwein is steaming hot and fragrant. A good indicator is when small bubbles start to form around the edges of the pot.
  5. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired, adding more sugar a tablespoon at a time until it reaches your preference.
  6. If using, stir in the brandy or rum just before serving.
  7. Strain the Glühwein through a fine-mesh sieve into a heatproof pitcher or directly into mugs to remove the spices and orange slices.
  8. Serve immediately in heatproof mugs, garnished with a fresh orange slice or a cinnamon stick if desired.

Tips

  • Never boil Glühwein, as this will cook off the alcohol and diminish the delicate flavors of the spices.
  • For a non-alcoholic version, substitute the red wine with cranberry juice or grape juice.
  • Feel free to experiment with other spices like cardamom pods, a few slices of fresh ginger, or a vanilla bean for added complexity.
